headline: Majors sit below their 200-day lines
paragraphs: The regime is uniform and severe. All seven majors sit below their 200-day moving averages, with Bitcoin 17% below and Ethereum, Solana, XRP, and ADA each 21% to 31% underwater. The golden cross has fired on six of seven (DOGE alone did not cross), which is a mechanical signal worth noting but arrives into an asset class already deep in structural decline. Bitcoin is down 51.9% from its 12-month high of $124,740; Ethereum down 64.1% from $4,691; Solana down 69.8% from $232.63; ADA down 83.5% from $0.87. These are not consolidations. These are bear regimes.

Momentum tells a sharper story. RSI-14 across the board sits in deep oversold: Bitcoin 22.5, Ethereum 18.4, Solana 15.5, XRP 17.3, BNB 18.9, DOGE 19.0, ADA 21.0. MACD sits below its signal line on every asset. Yet on the day, up +1.96% for Bitcoin, up +3.97% for Ethereum, up +2.31% for Solana, up +2.70% for XRP. This is a classic oversold bounce, not a trend reversal. Over the week, however, the picture inverts: Bitcoin down 6.24%, Ethereum down 15.18%, Solana down 12.85%, XRP down 19.36%. The divergence between today's bounce and the week's slide is exactly what oversold conditions produce. Watch whether the bounce holds or rolls over in the next few sessions.

Derivatives positioning reveals stress in the structure. Both are shorts being paid to hold, a sign that longs are expensive and unstable. Yet the long-to-short ratio for Bitcoin is 2.18 and for Ethereum 2.41, meaning longs outnumber shorts by more than two-to-one. Over nine hours, Ethereum shows $166k in longs and $204k in shorts, a rarer balance. SOL and XRP show heavy long liquidations too, though the windows are wider (11 and 12 hours). Shorts are being liquidated into what should be a falling asset, a signal that the bearish consensus has crowded.

Whale flows and stablecoin supply paint a bifurcated picture. Over the last 168 hours, Bitcoin moved $582M off exchanges while Ethereum moved $178M onto exchanges. The largest moves off were Bitcoin from Kraken, totaling $531M combined; the largest moves on were Ethereum to Binance ($162M) and Kraken ($149M). Meanwhile, stablecoins moved $494M onto exchanges, with the single largest move being $416M of USDT to Binance. This mix is not clean: whales pull Bitcoin to cold storage (a long-term holding posture), yet Ethereum and stablecoins arrive on exchange venues (preparation for trades or exits). The weekly trend supports this reading. The week ending Oct 31 saw $2.997B moved off exchanges; Nov 7 saw $4.125B off; Nov 14 saw $1.551B off. This week, Nov 21, the number has collapsed to $404M. The velocity of off-exchange movement is decelerating sharply, and stablecoin supply itself has fallen 6.2% over thirty days, sitting at $282.4B. The reserve of dry powder is tightening even as positioning remains long and leveraged.

Spot Bitcoin and Ethereum ETF flows are solidly negative and persistent. Bitcoin saw an outflow of $124.5M on the latest date (Nov 20) and a net outflow of $1,245.3M over five sessions, with same-direction movement on four of five days. Ethereum shows an outflow of $13.2M on the latest date and a net outflow of $221.7M over five sessions, with same-direction movement all five days. Traditional finance is not building conviction into this bounce; it is stepping aside. Fear and Greed sits at 11 (Extreme Fear), and the index has ranged only between 10 and 54 over the last thirty days, never clipping back into complacency.

The tape is showing a market in deep structural decline, undersold enough to bounce intraday, yet facing persistent outflows from regulated venues and stablecoin supply that is shrinking. The contradiction worth watching is whether Ethereum's move onto exchanges becomes a supply cascade for sale, and whether Bitcoin's cold storage accumulation persists or reverses. If off-exchange movement turns decisively negative and stablecoins stop flowing onto venues, the bounce has no fuel.
